context.guidance: Send Personal Data and Authentication Secrets in request bodies or headers, never in the path or query string, because URLs are written to logs, caches and browser history. Where an identifier must travel in a URL, use an opaque, short-lived token that reveals nothing about the Data Principal. This keeps the Rule 6(1)(a) protection intact on links that are logged and cached.

value.fix: Don't read the email from the query string (`query.email`). Have the client send it in the request body, for example with a POST/PUT and a JSON payload, and read it as `const { email } = body` (or `req.body.email`). Then remove the `email` query parameter from the route, the client calls and any generated links, so the email never shows up in URLs, server or proxy logs, caches or browser history. If a link really has to identify the user, such as a verification or unsubscribe link, put an opaque, random, short-lived, single-use token in the URL instead. Look the email up from that token on the server, and expire or delete the token after it's used. Also scrub any existing logs or analytics that captured the `email` query parameter.
